text:
Tampa Bay arrives at Buffalo having lost 4-3 at Winnipeg on Sunday, ending a three-game winning streak, though they're 3-1-1 in their last five. They're missing Brayden Point (16 points in 17 games), and going by how the coach has used them, Brandon Hagel is next in line for his minutes, with Anthony Cirelli the likeliest to move up on the power play. Buffalo, 3-2-0 in its last five, lost 4-1 to Vegas at home and is without Konsta Helenius, Justin Danforth and Matt Grzelcyk.

Our model leans slightly toward the Lightning, 3.29 expected goals to 2.98. Tampa Bay has taken 55% of the quality chances at five on five this season, Buffalo 51%, so there isn't much between them. The special-teams matchup to watch is the Lightning power play (0.78 expected goals a game) against a Sabres penalty kill that allows exactly that, and Buffalo takes 4.1 penalties a game.

In net, projected starters Andrei Vasilevskiy and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen are both below break-even this season (goals saved above expected of -0.42 and -1.11), but last year they were at +23.15 and +9.12. Luukkonen has been sharper lately, with 3.7 goals saved above expected over his last five starts. Nikita Kucherov is 82% for a point, and Hagel and Tage Thompson are each 37% to 38% to score. Our under-the-radar pick is Jack Quinn, 60% for a point, above his season pace, because his line creates chances. Cirelli also plays his 600th NHL game.
